messages.body_plain:
<https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-D9qbjx9ihMg/U4ryRxNtNiI/AAAAAAAAAMI/_be3UQ_dOv4/s1600/BulletGraphz_v_grey.png>

 <https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/-zEUZjeNqDFQ/U4ryO078ZII/AAAAAAAAAL8/jPOg5OzC8FU/s1600/BulletGraphz_h_grey.png>
Hi Tim,

the code here  <https://github.com/sipemu/BulletGraph>does what you want i.e. construct a bullet chart, although it is not interactive :-(. I'm sure there is an interactive R/NVD3 based one floating around somewhere on the web. Of course some form of interaction can be accomplished by using this code in Shiny. The only thing missing then is the animated part going from one state to another, which indeed is a cool thing ;-)

Here's the relevant code:

caveat: I'm not the author of this code

kind regards, Herman

#'  gridBulletGraphH: Horizontale Bullet Graph
#'
#'  @author Simon Müller
#'
#'  @param bgData:  data.frame with
#'                     measure  : label of what's being measured
#'                     unit     : label of units of the measure
#'                     high     : the high value for the measure
#'                     mean     : the mean value for the measure
#'                     low      : the low value for the measure
#'                     target   : the target value for the measure
#'                     value    : the actual value of the measure
#'
#'  @param nticks:  number of ticks. If single number all bullet graphs have the
#'                  same number of ticks, else a vector of nrow bgData is needed
#'
#'  @param format:  format of the ticks. Single or vector. Actually implemented:
#'                    s: standard (do nothing)
#'                    k: komma (decimal point, thousands komma)
#'                    d: point (vice verca to k)
#'                    p: add percent
#'
#'  @param bcol:    vector of colours
#'
#'  @param tcol:    colour of the target bar
#'
#'  @param vcol:    colour of the vertical bar
#'

gridBulletGraphH <- function(bgData, nticks=3, format="s", bcol=c("red", "yellow", "green"), tcol="black", vcol="black", font=25, scfont=15) {

  # Data Prep
  n <- nrow(bgData)
  nam <- c("low", "mean", "high", "target", "value")
  datMat <- as.matrix(bgData[, nam])

  # Nticks/Format Prep
  if (length(nticks) == 1) {
    nticks <- rep(nticks, n)
  }
  if (length(format) == 1) {
    format <- rep(format, n)
  }

  # Layout
  hl <- rep(1, n + 2)
  hu <- c("lines", rep("null", n), "lines")
  layout <- grid.layout(n + 2, 4, widths = unit(c(1, 1, 5, 2), c("lines", "null", "null", "lines")),
                        heights = unit(hl, hu))

  # Set Layout
  grid.newpage()
  pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout = layout))
  for (i in 1:n) {
    #
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = i+1,
                   layout.pos.col = 3)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 3,
                             ncol    = 1,
                             heights = unit(c(1, 2, 1), c("null", "null", "null")))
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 2,
                   layout.pos.col = 1,
                   xscale         = c(0, datMat[i, 3]))
    pushViewport(vp)

    # x-Axis Labels
    # Formatierung Label
    if (format[i] == "s") {
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
    } else if (format[i] == "p"){
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
      labels <- paste0(labels, "%")
    } else if (format[i] == "k") {
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
      labels <- format(labels, digits=10, nsmall=0, decimal.mark=".", big.mark=",")
    }

    grid.xaxis(at=brks, label=labels, gp=gpar(fontsize=scfont, col="black", fontface="bold"))

    grid.rect(x      = c(0, datMat[i, 1:2]) / datMat[i, 3],
              width  = unit(diff(c(0, datMat[i, 1:3])), "native"),
              y      = rep(0.5, 3),
              height = 1,
              just   = "left",
              gp     = gpar(fill=bcol, col=bcol))

    grid.rect(x      = c(0, datMat[i, 5]),
              width  = unit(diff(c(0, datMat[i, 5])), "native"),
              y      = 0.5,
              height = 0.5,
              gp     = gpar(fill=vcol, col=vcol), just="left")

    a <- datMat[i, 3] * 0.005
    grid.rect(x      = datMat[i, 4] / datMat[i, 3],
              width  = unit(a, "native"),
              y      = 0.5,
              height = 0.8,
              gp     = gpar(fill=tcol, col=tcol), just="left")

    upViewport(n=3)

    # Annotation
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=layout))
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = i+1,
                   layout.pos.col = 2)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout 1: Same layout as graph
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 3,
                             ncol    = 1,
                             heights = unit(c(1, 2, 1), c("null", "null", "null")))
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 2,
                   layout.pos.col = 1)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout 2: two rows of text; centred middle of graph
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 2,
                             ncol    = 1,
                             heights = unit(c(1, 1), c("null", "null")))
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    # First Text: Measure
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 1,
                   layout.pos.col = 1)
    pushViewport(vp)
    grid.text(label = bgData$measure[i],
              just  = "right",
              gp    = gpar(fontsize=font, col="black", fontface="bold"),
              x     = .9,
              y     = .5)
    upViewport()

    # Second Text: Unit
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 2,
                   layout.pos.col = 1)
    pushViewport(vp)
    grid.text(label = bgData$units[i],
              just  = "right",
              gp    = gpar(fontsize=font, col="black"),
              x     = .9,
              y     = .5)
    upViewport(n=5)
  }
}

#'  gridBulletGraphV: Vertical Bullet Graph
#'
#'  @author Simon Müller
#'
#'  @param bgData:  data.frame with
#'                     measure  : label of what's being measured
#'                     unit     : label of units of the measure
#'                     high     : the high value for the measure
#'                     mean     : the mean value for the measure
#'                     low      : the low value for the measure
#'                     target   : the target value for the measure
#'                     value    : the actual value of the measure
#'
#'  @param nticks:  number of ticks. If single number all bullet graphs have the
#'                  same number of ticks, else a vector of nrow bgData is needed
#'
#'  @param format:  format of the ticks. Single or vector. Actually implemented:
#'                    s: standard (do nothing)
#'                    k: komma (decimal point, thousands komma)
#'                    d: point (vice verca to k)
#'                    p: add percent
#'
#'  @param bcol:    vector of colours
#'
#'  @param tcol:    colour of the target bar
#'
#'  @param vcol:    colour of the vertical bar
#'

gridBulletGraphV <- function(bgData, nticks=3, format="s", bcol=c("red", "yellow", "green"), tcol="black", vcol="black", font=25, scfont=15) {

  # Data Prep
  n <- nrow(bgData)
  nam <- c("low", "mean", "high", "target", "value")
  datMat <- as.matrix(bgData[, nam])

  # Nticks/Format Prep
  if (length(nticks) == 1) {
    nticks <- rep(nticks, n)
  }
  if (length(format) == 1) {
    format <- rep(format, n)
  }

  # Layout
  hl <- rep(1, n + 2)
  hu <- c("lines", rep("null", n), "lines")
  layout <- grid.layout(4, n + 2, widths = unit(hl, hu),
                        heights = unit(c(1, 1, 5, 2), c("lines", "null", "null", "lines")))

  # Set Layout
  grid.newpage()
  pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout = layout))
  for (i in 1:n) {
    #
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 3,
                   layout.pos.col = i+1)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 1,
                             widths  = unit(c(1, 2, 1), c("null", "null", "null")),
                             ncol    = 3)
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 1,
                   layout.pos.col = 2,
                   yscale         = c(0, datMat[i, 3]))
    pushViewport(vp)

    # x-Axis Labels
    # Formatierung Label
    if (format[i] == "s") {
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
    } else if (format[i] == "p"){
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
      labels <- paste0(labels, "%")
    } else if (format[i] == "k") {
      brks <- labels <- round(seq(0, datMat[i, 3], length=nticks[i]), 0)
      labels <- format(labels, digits=10, nsmall=0, decimal.mark=".", big.mark=",")
    }

    grid.yaxis(at=brks, label=labels, gp=gpar(fontsize=scfont, col="black", fontface="bold"))

    grid.rect(y      = c(0, datMat[i, 1:2]) / datMat[i, 3],
              height = unit(diff(c(0, datMat[i, 1:3])), "native"),
              x      = rep(0.5, 3),
              width  = 1,
              just   = "bottom",
              gp     = gpar(fill=bcol, col=bcol))

    grid.rect(y      = c(0, datMat[i, 5]),
              height = unit(diff(c(0, datMat[i, 5])), "native"),
              x      = 0.5,
              width  = 0.5,
              gp     = gpar(fill=vcol, col=vcol), just="bottom")

    a <- datMat[i, 1] * 0.01
    grid.rect(y      = datMat[i, 4] / datMat[i, 3],
              height = unit(a, "native"),
              x      = 0.5,
              width  = 0.8,
              gp     = gpar(fill=tcol, col=tcol), just="bottom")

    upViewport(n=3)

    # Annotation
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=layout))
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 2,
                   layout.pos.col = i+1)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout 1: Same layout as graph
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 1,
                             ncol    = 3,
                             widths  = unit(c(1, 2, 1), c("null", "null", "null")))
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 1,
                   layout.pos.col = 2)
    pushViewport(vp)

    # Sublayout 2: two rows of text; centred middle of graph
    subLayout <- grid.layout(nrow    = 2,
                             ncol    = 1,
                             widths = unit(c(1, 1), c("null", "null")))
    pushViewport(plotViewport(c(0, 0, 0, 0), layout=subLayout))

    # First Text: Measure
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 1,
                   layout.pos.col = 1)
    pushViewport(vp)
    grid.text(label = bgData$measure[i],
              just  = "bottom",
              gp    = gpar(fontsize=font, col="black", fontface="bold"),
              x     = .5,
              y     = 0.1)
    upViewport()

    # Second Text: Unit
    vp <- viewport(layout.pos.row = 2,
                   layout.pos.col = 1)
    pushViewport(vp)
    grid.text(label = bgData$units[i],
              just  = "bottom",
              gp    = gpar(fontsize=font, col="black"),
              x     = .5,
              y     = .5)
    upViewport(n=5)
  }
}

###
### example
###

ytd2005 <- data.frame(
  measure=c("Revenue", "Profit", "Avg Order Size", "New Customers", "Cust Satisfaction"),
  units=c("U.S. $ (1,000s)", "%", "U.S. $", "Count", "Top Rating of 5"),
  low=c(150, 20, 350, 1400, 3.5),
  mean=c(225, 25, 500, 2000, 4.25),
  high=c(300, 30, 600, 2500, 5),
  target=c(250, 26, 550, 2100, 4.2),
  value=c(275, 22.5, 310, 1700, 4.5)
)

nticks <- c(7, 7, 7, 6, 7)
format <- c("s", "p", "s", "k", "s")

col1 <- c("#a5a7a9", "#c5c6c8", "#e6e6e7")
png("BulletGraphz_h_grey.png", width=1500, height=500)

library(grid)
gridBulletGraphH(ytd2005, nticks=nticks, format=format, bcol=col1)
dev.off()

png("BulletGraphz_v_grey.png", width=1500, height=500)
gridBulletGraphV(ytd2005, nticks=nticks, format=format, bcol=col1)
dev.off()

I've faced the same error (Shiny 0.9.1), and after some analysis of the shiny source code&documentation I was able to find a solution.

Simple creation of empty file named DESCRIPTION (Linux: touch DESCRIPTION) solved my problem.

Thanks,

messages.body_plain:
I haven't followed the group here too much lately, so maybe this is already a thing:

I run into a number of scenarios where I have implemented reactive functions that output smallish data frames that are then connected to output on the client-side. For example, I may have a textInput that allows a user to type in a search term... that search term then activates a reactive function that queries a MySQL db and makes a smallish data frame available (say, 2x20) on the server-side... this activates a selectInput update that is reflected on the client-side... and when the user then selects from that updated selectInput, the selection has to go back to the server and activate some reactive process before the user sees the product. Is there any way to send/store small datasets (like the 2x20 data frame I stated here) on the client-side, so that I can save that trip to the server?

Is what I'm asking here (if possible) bad practice for any reason?

Thanks!

Dan

Hi Dharmendra,

This is actually an RStudio issue (rather than a Shiny issue) and I encourage you to post it over on our RStudio open-source support forum at https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/topics for the best possible support.

That being said, typically this is an error that R is unable to contact the png device from within RStudio - you should check and see if the same commands work within R itself rather than RStudio. If they don't, its likely an issue with how you've compiled R and you need to make sure you've compiled it with png support.

You can also try running the following commands:
sessionInfo()
capabilities()
png(); dev.off()
x11()
Sys.getenv("DISPLAY")
in both RStudio and R and let us know on the support forums what your results are - that will help us troubleshoot what's going on here.

Thanks,
Ian

messages.subject_clean: client-side reactivity - sending/storing small data sets on the client-side
messages.body_plain:
You can store values on the client side just by assigning them to global variables--but you have to do both the storing and the reading from JavaScript, it's not clear from your question if that's something you're trying to avoid.

In general though Shiny assumes that roundtrips between the client and server are relatively fast. Maybe not fast enough for e.g. 30fps animations being driven by the server, but certainly using a selectInput to drive an output should be OK. If you're actually observing unacceptable latency when you're doing that, rather than just bothered by the idea of that extra roundtrip, then let's definitely talk about it.

messages.subject: Shiny 0.10.0
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.10.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We’re hoping to submit Shiny 0.10.0 to CRAN shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we’ve added since 0.9.1. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub (the version number is still 0.9.1.x there but will eventually become 0.10.0 on CRAN):

if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')
Shiny Docs

Many of you are familiar with knitr <http://yihui.name/knitr/> and R Markdown <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>, excellent tools for creating documents that combine R code and output with your writing.

With Shiny 0.10 and R Markdown v2, you can easily embed Shiny inputs and outputs, and even entire Shiny applications, right into your R Markdown documents! You can now create documents that allow your readers to change the assumptions underlying your analysis and see the results immediately. R Markdown documents with Shiny apps or widgets embedded are called Shiny Docs.

Shiny Docs combine the expressiveness of R Markdown with the interactivity of Shiny. These documents can be run locally on the desktop or be deployed to ShinyApps <http://shinyapps.io> or Shiny Server <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/shiny-server/> v1.2.

To start writing Shiny Docs, just install the current preview release <http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/preview/> of RStudio (v0.98.891) as it includes not only updated versions of the various packages required to run Shiny Docs (including Shiny 0.10) but also tools for previewing and iterative development.

Learn more about Shiny Docs here <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html>.
Server-side processing for selectize input

The client-side selectize input (introduced in shiny 0.9.0) relies solely on JavaScript to process searching on typing. The server-side selectize input uses R to process searching, and R will return the filtered data to selectize. To use the server version, you need to create a selectize instance in the UI, and update it to the server version:

# in ui.R
selectizeInput('foo', choices = NULL, ...)

# in server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = data, server = TRUE)
})

The server-side processing is particularly useful when the number of choices is very large. For example, when there are 100,000 choices for the selectize input, it will be slow to write and load all of them at once on a page. With the new server-side selectize features, you can start from an empty selectize input, and only fetch the choices that the user searches for, which can be much faster. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html> for more information and examples.
New layout functions

Three new functions, flowLayout(), splitLayout(), and inputPanel(), were added for putting UI elements side by side.
flowPanel() lays out its children in a left-to-right, top-to-bottom arrangement.
splitLayout() evenly divides its horizontal space among its children (or unevenly divides if cellWidths argument is provided).
inputPanel() is like flowPanel(), but with a light grey background, and is intended for encapsulating small input controls wherever vertical space is at a premium.

A new argument inline (TRUE/FALSE) was also added to checkboxGroupInput() and radioButtons() to arrange check boxes and radio buttons horizontally.
Custom validation error messages

Sometimes you do not want your render functions in server.R to proceed unless certain input conditions are satisfied, e.g. the action button has been clicked, or a select input value has been chosen. In these cases, you may want to either stop the render function quietly, or with a custom message. In shiny 0.10.0, we introduced the functions validate() and need() to specify the validation conditions. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html> for details and examples.

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS> file. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.

Thanks for your support – we look forward to hearing from you!

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server - Is sky the limit?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Enzo,

Memory wise, on Shiny Server Open Source it is one R process per app, and that one process can potentially serve many users. Whether objects are duplicated for each user or shared across users depends on where you define them; see this article for details:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

With Shiny Server Pro it is the same except you're not limited to one R process per app. Each of the multiple R processes per app can serve many users.

Yes, Shiny Server Pro (and Open Source for that matter) work with AWS and ELB. Make sure you enable sticky sessions in ELB.

<https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/-0gngVIA7DTA/U4-Y9BlcZII/AAAAAAAAAM4/mpIDSUku7z8/s1600/welcome.png>

Hi,

one solution is to use a modal <http://getbootstrap.com/2.3.2/javascript.html#modals>. I made a small shiny app for you which displays a welcome message to the user in this way. After you close it you end up in the 'normal' app. Obviously if the welcome page is a real part of the application you can go back to, it can just be a tab in a tab panel. On the other hand, if it is a one time moment in the use of your app a modal may be an option.

The modal can be included using the ShinyBS  <https://github.com/ebailey78/shinyBS>package, which offers various nice extensions to the basic shiny framework. You can completely customize the modal e.g. you can make the modal full screen by changing the associated css  <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/css.html>rules, add a background etc. I included an example of how to do just that.

The modal addition in shinyBS is quite new, to use it install the development version of shinyBS:

install.packages("devtools")
install_github("shinyBS", "ebailey78")

Below the ui.r and server.r scripts of the toy app. The app itself allows you to sort a table by a column and save the result (I shamelessly copied that part from one of the other Shiny group users ;-)

Hope this helps, best Herman
the Netherlands

###
### ui.r
###

library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

    # add a button to open the modal
    bsButton("moTrig", "open Modal", style = "primary"),

    # a simple modal
    bsModal("moMod", "Welcome message", trigger = "moTrig",
          tags$head(
                tags$style(HTML("
                 .modal{
                  width: 90%;
                  left: 5%;
                  margin-left:auto;
                  margin-right:auto;
                  height: auto;
                }
                .modal-body {
                  color: white;
                  background-image:url('http://www.designbolts.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/Free-Topographic-Map-Seamless-pattern.jpg');
                }
            "))
          ),

        h1("Hello, welcome to shiny")
    ),

    # below some code to be able to download a filtered table object
    # that is, the user performs some filtering on the table by manual actions
    # after which you can download the table in
    tags$head(
        tags$style(type="text/css", "tfoot {display: table-header-group}")
    ),

    titlePanel("Filtered Data CSV Download"),
        sidebarLayout(
            sidebarPanel(
                HTML('
                    <script type="text/javascript">
                        $(document).ready(function() {
                            $("#downloadData").click(function() {
                                var filtered_table_data = $("#DataTables_Table_0").dataTable()._("tr", {"filter":"applied"});
                                Shiny.onInputChange("filtered_table", filtered_table_data);
                            });
                        });
                   </script>
                '),

                downloadButton('downloadData', 'Download Filtered Data')
            ),
            mainPanel(
                dataTableOutput("data_table")
            )
        )
))

###
### server.r
###

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    # open the modal on opening the shiny app
    toggleModal(session, "moMod")

    # below the code for the table example
    Dataset <- reactive({
        df <- mtcars
        df[is.na <http://is.na>(df)] <- ""
        return(df)
    })

    output$data_table <- renderDataTable({
        Dataset()
    }, options = list(sDom = "ilftpr",iDisplayLength = 10))

    ProcessedFilteredData <- reactive({
        v <- input$filtered_table
        col_names <- names(Dataset())
        n_cols <- length(col_names)
        n_row <- length(v)/n_cols
        m <- matrix(v, ncol = n_cols, byrow = TRUE)
        df <- data.frame(m)
        names(df) <- col_names
        return(df)
    })

    output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
        filename = function() { 'filtered_data.csv' }, content = function(file) {
            write.csv(ProcessedFilteredData(), file, row.names = FALSE)
        }
    )
})

messages.body_plain:
Ok, thanks to the app gallery, you guys did a great job of putting some cool code that are super great to learn the intricacies of shiny, but bottom line, I figure out an easy way to save the state of a selection through changes in the UI.

here is the bits that does the magic. It uses a reactiveValues() and an observer({}) block to watch and update the state of the reactiveValues(). Not really easy to pick up at first but I make sense when you think about it. here it is (I would be very happy to get comments on whether this is the shiny way or not...)

    ## Remember the selected samples
    exps <- reactiveValues()
    observe({
        ## If no orders are selected, just return, whipping off the values in the exps list
        if (is.null(input$samples)){
            if (!is.null(input$order)){
                exps[[input$order]] <- NULL
            }
            return()
        }
        isolate({
            exps[[input$order]] <- input$samples
        })
    })

messages.subject: Re: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
messages.subject_clean: osmar library conflict (openstreetmap parsing)
messages.body_plain:
Since osmar also has the tags object (as a function, or what R calls
"closure"), it overrides the tags object in shiny when you
library(osmar). The solution is to make sure you use the one in shiny
via shiny::tags$hr.

Please also note there may be other objects that are overridden by
osmar, such as `span` in geosphere, one of the dependencies of osmar.
When you see objects are masked by another package, you will have to
use package::object.

> library(shiny)
> library(osmar)
Loading required package: XML
Loading required package: RCurl
Loading required package: bitops
Loading required package: geosphere
Loading required package: sp

Attaching package: 'geosphere'

The following object is masked from 'package:shiny':

    span

Attaching package: 'osmar'

The following object is masked from 'package:utils':

    find

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Wow, you've gotten impressively far for 2 weeks! You shouldn't need the jQuery at all. Instead, when you call updateSelectedInput, pass a named vector for choices; the name will be used as the label, and the value will be used as the value. In this case, if it's the index that you want, then you can use something like: choices <- 1:nrow(business_list()) names(choices) <- business_list()$name updateSelectInput(session, "search_result", choices = c( if (business_list()$name[1] != "No result") c("Please select a restaurant"=""), choices )) Then the value in input$search_result will be a row number (as a string, unfortunately for this case) instead of a name. You might also create a reactive like this: selected_business <- reactive({ if (input$search_result == "") return(NULL) return(business_list()[as.numeric(input$search_result),]) }) Then everywhere else you can simply do selected_business()$image_b, etc. On Fri, Jun 6, 2014 at 11:15 AM, Ryan Hojeong Seo wrote: > Hi, I am a total newbie when it comes to programming. > I am trying to make an }) > > get_business_data <- reactive({ > if (input$searchAction == 0) return() > if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return() > if (input$selIdx == 0) return() > withProgress(session, min=0, max=10, { > setProgress(message="Downloading reviews", > detail="This may take a while...") > data <- get_data(business_list()$id[input$selIdx]) > for (i in 1:50) { > setProgress(value = i) > } > return(data) > }) > }) > > observe({ > if (input$searchAction == 0) return() > updateSelectInput(session, > "search_result", > "", > c(if(business_list()$name[1] != "No result") "Please select a restaurant", > messages.subject: Running cron jobsof R scripts together with Shiny Server
messages.subject_clean: Running cron jobsof R scripts together with Shiny Server
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

We have a server that has a cron job downloading data every hour from some source through the Internet and into a database (in the same server) using R scripts.
We are developing a Shiny app that uses this data in some way. At some point, there will be around 5 users probably at any given time.
Our intention is to have everything (cron jobs with scripts, database, Shiny Server) in the same server. We want to start using the open source version of Shiny server.

Based on these discussions:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/cron$20job/shiny-discuss/uxXsxwkW00s/eG-ICORa-ygJ
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/cron$20job/shiny-discuss/MpnqXKhqnnw/Zk6PNkYBULQJ
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/cron$20job/shiny-discuss/d_KI2gf7ZC0/YUeOyfrTzjEJ

it seem for us that this is actually possible. We are just wondering what happens when the cron job executes: does it create a new rsession? does it "interrupt" the ones that are running Shiny?
The execution itself takes a couple of minutes to retrieve and write all the relevant data.

We just want to be sure that it is compatible to run R scripts in a server while it is running Shiny apps so we do not get surprises when installing Shiny Server.

thanks!

condition is NA.

Error in if (NA) 1 : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

The reason that the file size is NA is probably that the file does not
exist. You may need to check file.exists() first.

messages.subject_clean: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
messages.body_plain:
One reason for the locale being C is that the environment variable
LANG is unset. You may check that using Sys.getenv('LANG') in R, or in
a terminal:

$ echo $LANG
en_US.utf8

If that is the case, one solution is to define LANG=C.UTF-8 or
en_US.UTF-8 in Renviron.site (depending what locales are available:
`locale -a`), so R can pick up a locale that is appropriate for
Unicode characters.

Regards,
Yihui

The following helps, but it could lead to problems.

# global.R
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO_PANDOC")))
  Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC = "/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/pandoc")

Dieter

messages.subject: Re: Announcing shinyFiles package
messages.subject_clean: Announcing shinyFiles package
messages.body_plain:
Just a quick update to those interested.

shinyFiles has now been submitted to CRAN and should hopefully be available soon.

New features since last post:
File sorting: Files can now be sorted by name, type, size, creation and modification date.
Volumes: Support for multiple different roots to emulate different volumes on the file system. Furthermore a utility function getVolumes() that automatically detects the volumes available on the system.
Responsive: The file chooser now responds to changes in the file system. Plug in a USB drive and see it appear in the list of available volumes; Delete a file on the host computer and see it disappear from the file chooser.
As always type: shinyFilesExample() for a simple example of the file chooser.

best

Thomas

Den fredag den 23. maj 2014 13.37.17 UTC+2 skrev Thomas Lin Pedersen:
> Hi All
>
> I'm happy to announce the availability of my new shiny extension package 'shinyFiles'.
>
> The purpose of the package is to make a server side file navigator available to shiny app developers, comparable to the given with the fileInput() function. The use cases are mostly the following:
> When an app is intended to run locally, the use of fileInput gives an unnecessary overhead by requiring selected files to be copied to a temporary location before being made available to the server script. This is of little concern with small files, but as the file sizes approach the Gb range it gets unacceptable. shinyFiles solves this by directly exposing the file system and making the full path of selected files available without copying.
> In some circumstances It might make sense to expose a subset of the server file system to the user in remote running apps (selecting old results or configuration files etc.). shinyFiles allow the developer to restrict the client access to a certain subdirectory of the full file system, by specifying a starting root, beyond which the client have no access. Furthermore subdirectories of the root can be removed as well as file-types to give fine-grained control over what is exposed to the client.
> The functionality is designed to be extremely simple to implement, and makes it easy to toggle between fileInput and shinyFiles. If you're designing your html from scratch it only requires the addition of a single <button> element to make it work.
>
> The visual side is designed to look great on bootstrap pages, but can be customised to your own needs. Furthermore the icons can be customised if you have your own icon set...
>
> At the moment it is only available on github (use devtools to install), but it should be submitted to cran after some further testing. After installation you can run shinyFilesExample() to be presented with a minimal app showing the functionality.
>
> I would welcome any feedback.
>
> best
>
> Thomas
>
>  <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-Xb0rH0Gh7HY/U38yrkHfEPI/AAAAAAAAD2c/dux5aXFHie8/s1600/Screen+Shot+2014-05-23+at+13.17.43.png>
>

messages.subject: Re: Bullet charts using NVD3 js
messages.subject_clean: Bullet charts using NVD3 js
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Interesting thread growing here. Apologies for not writing sooner.
With regards to Bullet charts and shiny, I managed to get this up and running in a not so obvious way.

My recommendation to get bullets (or in fact any sort of charting) up and running is going native on the libraries.
If you are wanting to get a nice UI with a few charts - I found this was quite clunky and slow going with Wrapper libraries with R so instead I went with the following: (I set up my shiny box using Ubuntu server with AWS)

- Instead of using ui.R I set up the native libraries for nvd3, d3 etc in folders like www/css and www/js
- I then wrote some Rscripts and cron jobs that use R libraries like jsonlite to format the data (csv/ json)
- I found charting like Bullets in NVD3 or any other sort of visualisation you want to use are much faster as well with this approach.

Disclaimers: I am awful at front end coding (not my day job) but it was not too hard to set up a bootstrap framework to get the charts to be responsive and nicely nested in columns and rows.

Unfortunately I cannot share this code as I run it at my work but will find some time to create a demo version of it and will put it up on github. Let me know if you guys have any questions/ suggestions about this workflow - can't say it is elegant as I am still very much experimenting with it all, but it works really well :)

cheers,
Narbeh Y.

Yes, it works! Thank you so much Joe.

Anyone, who wants to try Joe's code, can just run the code below..
---
runApp(list( ui = fluidPage(
  tabsetPanel(id = "tabset",
              tabPanel(value = "tab1", "One"),
              tabPanel(value = "tab2", "Two"),
              tabPanel(value = "insight", "Three")
  )
), server = function(input, output, session) {
  # On startup, read the URL parameter
  queryParams <- parseQueryString(isolate(session$clientData$url_search))
  if ('tab' %in% names(queryParams))
    updateTabsetPanel(session, 'tabset', selected = paste0('tab', queryParams[['tab']]))
}))

messages.subject: Bundle apps for local install
messages.subject_clean: Bundle apps for local install
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

How may we bundle a shiny app with R and the shiny package for convenient download and installation by non R users? We need a user (that does not know or use R) to be able to click on a web link. In response an installer downloads and installs everything they need to run the R Shiny app, relatively seamlessly. Kind of like we would do if we wrote an app in visual basic.

It's not good enough to just put all the ui.R and server.R code into one larger .R file (I've seen examples of this), and send it to them. They do not have R installed and walking every potential user through installing R and the packages is a barrier to adaptation. We really need it self contained. One last reason to do it this way, is to control the version of R and shiny that is used to run the app, by bundling R and shiny with the app.

Jonathan

Okay, we are trying to put an end to this never-ending encoding
problem under Windows now, and we will really appreciate it if you can
help us test it:

  if (!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")
  devtools::install_github("yihui/shiny@bugfix/windows-encoding")

Note you do not need to set options(encoding="UTF-8") (that may lead
to undesired effects on other I/O functions in R). The only thing you
need to make sure is ui.R/server.R must be UTF8 encoded, which you
have already done in your gist.

Please also note this is still experimental, meaning it is subject to
further changes.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
This error message seems to indicate that the WebSocket could not
decode the message. From my experience, this means the message
probably contained multi-byte characters that were not appropriately
encoded, which could be a consequence of a locale bug that we recently
discovered and fixed in Shiny Server. If possible, please test a more
recent version of the Shiny Server:
https://s3.amazonaws.com/rstudio-shiny-server-os-build/ubuntu-12.04/x86_64/shiny-server-1.2.0.355-amd64.deb
Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

On Friday, June 13, 2014 5:54:41 AM UTC-7, Jonathan wrote:
> Hello,
>
> How may we bundle a shiny app with R and the shiny package for convenient download and installation by non R users? We need a user (that does not know or use R) to be able to click on a web link. In response an installer downloads and installs everything they need to run the R Shiny app, relatively seamlessly. Kind of like we would do if we wrote an app in visual basic.
>
> It's not good enough to just put all the ui.R and server.R code into one larger .R file (I've seen examples of this), and send it to them. They do not have R installed and walking every potential user through installing R and the packages is a barrier to adaptation. We really need it self contained. One last reason to do it this way, is to control the version of R and shiny that is used to run the app, by bundling R and shiny with the app.
>
> Jonathan

I just updated most of my app to use session$sendCustomMessage() instead of relying on custom outputs to send data to the client. This seems to remove the problem. messages.body_plain:
Might the issue be that all outputs are held and "flushed" at the same time? In other words, if a new value for input x is sent from the client, and outputs a, b, and c all depend (directly or indirectly) on it, then they are all executed serially but only sent to the client when the last one completes. This is in contrast to sendCustomMessage, which goes immediately. (I was always prepared for this to be a controversial decision and we could do work to make this a per-output option, but it comes up surprisingly little)

The work required to maintain the reactive graph is miniscule in most cases, and shouldn't be related to the size of the data being sent around.

messages.subject_clean: Connecting Shiny server front end to node.js backend files
messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server is implemented in node.js but not designed to be extended directly with your own node.js code. However, what you could do is put another server in front of it, written in node.js, go, or whatever, and proxy requests intended for shiny server to your shiny-server instance. That's a really nice thing about HTTP servers/proxies, they compose very nicely.

Just be aware that your proxying logic ideally will support not only HTTP but also WebSockets. Or you could disable websockets in shiny-server, then you'd only need to proxy HTTP--this would just be a little less efficient but otherwise should work OK (it's what we currently do on ShinyApps.io).

messages.subject: Re: mclapply
messages.subject_clean: mclapply
messages.body_plain:
I think this may be an inherent limitation of mclapply. From the docs:
"mclapply is a parallelized version of lapply, but there is an important difference: mclapply does not affect the calling environment in any way, the only side-effect is the delivery of the result (with the exception of a fall-back to lapply when there is only one core)."

A little background: A function without side effects is one that takes an input and returns an output without affecting anything else. A function with a side effect alters the external environment in some way -- for example, if a function modifies a global variable, that's a side effect.

In the case of Shiny, the way that a reactive expression or observer takes a dependency on another reactive object is via side effects -- the evaluation of input$nmbr alters the state of the input$nmbr so that it knows to invalidate the reactive expression when its value changes.

My understanding is that mclapply doesn't have side effects because it spawns a new process for each run, and the new processes can't affect the state of the original process.

I think you should be able to work around this by simply evaluating input$nmbr outside of the mclapply, like this:

haz_test <- reactive({
  input$nmbr # Take a dependency on this

  analysis_test( ..., input$nmbr, session)
})

-Winston

messages.subject: sliderInput is hard to use on a draggable flixedPanel, depending on where the panel is.
messages.subject_clean: sliderInput is hard to use on a draggable flixedPanel, depending on where the panel is.
messages.body_plain:
I am working on an app that plots points on a leaflet map. So far everything works well, but I would like to add a slider which helps control the radius of the points. I am using the shiny-leaflet library by Joe Cheng and his "SuperZip" example as a model. The points on the map are really circles added using map$addCircle and the slider is to help control the radius argument.

I put the sliderInput on a fixed panel that is draggable (similar to the one on SuperZip). However there is an issue. If I drag the panel to the left side of the display everything works great. If I drag it to the right side, it is nearly impossible to use the slider. I cannot "grag" the slider tool, and if I do, moving the hand a long way only moves the slider one notch. If I put the panel in the middle of the display, then it works, but poorly. You can grab the slider tool, but to go select the right most value (my slider is 1 to 4)   you need to move the hand all the way to the right of the display, which is far past the end of the slider.

If I get time I will try to make a reproducible version and log it as an issue on github, but I am hoping someone here has a work around or at least a theory as to what the problem is.

JP

messages.subject: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
messages.subject_clean: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a functioning app which works fine locally via runApp() on Windows, as well as on our own hosting of shiny server (Shiny Server v1.0.0.42 and Node.js v0.10.21). I tab through various tabset panels to display different plots without issue. However, on Spark, all tabs remain blank. No plotting occurs. This distinction occurred with version 0.9 but I have upgraded all three to 0.10 and it is the same. Not sure what went wrong because it used to work on Spark as well. It may be related to a supplemental package. I also use shinyAce and shinyRGL.

I noticed with shinyRGL, upon upgrading to shiny version 0.10 I had to move the library(shinyRGL) command from server.R to global.R or the app could not find webGLOutput(). This global placement was not required before. But that was a separate problem. Upon moving that line of code to global.R I was once again able to run the app locally, on our shiny server instance, and on Spark. And this returned me to the original problem of absent plot reactivity on Spark only.

http://spark.rstudio.com/uafsnap/plot3D/
The About tab and the R Code tab work fine. The six plot tabs do nothing. But again, this is only on Spark. They work fine on other systems. I have tried in Firefox and Chrome. Same results. Also, websockets are disabled on our shiny server just like on Spark.

Code is public:
https://github.com/ua-snap/shiny-apps/tree/master/plot3D

Thanks,
Matt

Base R does not support directly support https connections, and you
will have to rely on system tools such as wget/curl or RCurl to
download files from https connections. Or if you are under Windows,
you need the setInternet2() function.

In shiny, you can certainly provide certain files for users to
download. Please search for "download" in the gallery for examples:

messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.10.0
messages.body_plain:
Server side selectize really helped me out - I had thousands of options for two of my inputs.  Combined with Joe's leaflet code, I could make my app that explores salary data for different job titles:

http://www.wagemap.com/salaries/

Maybe this is a selectize issue and not a shiny issue, but it's hard to populate the selectizeInput with a default value.  Since the input options aren't updated until after you start typing, it looks like there's only one default option in the drop down, which is misleading.  I made the compromise of just leaving the choices as null, forcing the user to start typing and seeing the whole list.

You guys keep rolling out features just as I need them (datatables also had perfect timing).  Keep up the good work!

On Wednesday, June 4, 2014 10:46:37 AM UTC-7, Yihui Xie wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> We’re hoping to submit Shiny 0.10.0 to CRAN shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we’ve added since 0.9.1. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub (the version number is still 0.9.1.x there but will eventually become 0.10.0 on CRAN):
> if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')
> devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')
> Shiny Docs
>
> Many of you are familiar with knitr <http://yihui.name/knitr/> and R Markdown <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>, excellent tools for creating documents that combine R code and output with your writing.
>
> With Shiny 0.10 and R Markdown v2, you can easily embed Shiny inputs and outputs, and even entire Shiny applications, right into your R Markdown documents! You can now create documents that allow your readers to change the assumptions underlying your analysis and see the results immediately. R Markdown documents with Shiny apps or widgets embedded are called Shiny Docs.
>
> Shiny Docs combine the expressiveness of R Markdown with the interactivity of Shiny. These documents can be run locally on the desktop or be deployed to ShinyApps <http://shinyapps.io> or Shiny Server <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/shiny-server/> v1.2.
>
> To start writing Shiny Docs, just install the current preview release <http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/preview/> of RStudio (v0.98.891) as it includes not only updated versions of the various packages required to run Shiny Docs (including Shiny 0.10) but also tools for previewing and iterative development.
>
> Learn more about Shiny Docs here <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html>.
> Server-side processing for selectize input
>
> The client-side selectize input (introduced in shiny 0.9.0) relies solely on JavaScript to process searching on typing. The server-side selectize input uses R to process searching, and R will return the filtered data to selectize. To use the server version, you need to create a selectize instance in the UI, and update it to the server version:
> # in ui.R
> selectizeInput('foo', choices = NULL, ...)
>
> # in server.R
> shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
>   updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = data, server = TRUE)
> })
>
> The server-side processing is particularly useful when the number of choices is very large. For example, when there are 100,000 choices for the selectize input, it will be slow to write and load all of them at once on a page. With the new server-side selectize features, you can start from an empty selectize input, and only fetch the choices that the user searches for, which can be much faster. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html> for more information and examples.
> New layout functions
>
> Three new functions, flowLayout(), splitLayout(), and inputPanel(), were added for putting UI elements side by side.
> flowPanel() lays out its children in a left-to-right, top-to-bottom arrangement.
> splitLayout() evenly divides its horizontal space among its children (or unevenly divides if cellWidths argument is provided).
> inputPanel() is like flowPanel(), but with a light grey background, and is intended for encapsulating small input controls wherever vertical space is at a premium.
>
> A new argument inline (TRUE/FALSE) was also added to checkboxGroupInput() and radioButtons() to arrange check boxes and radio buttons horizontally.
> Custom validation error messages
>
> Sometimes you do not want your render functions in server.R to proceed unless certain input conditions are satisfied, e.g. the action button has been clicked, or a select input value has been chosen. In these cases, you may want to either stop the render function quietly, or with a custom message. In shiny 0.10.0, we introduced the functions validate() and need() to specify the validation conditions. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html> for details and examples.
>
> There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS> file. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.
>
> Thanks for your support – we look forward to hearing from you!

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

First off shiny is a really fantastic tool and much appreciated.

I'm running into some unusual repainting issues using a JS plotting library in conjunction with shiny server.

Specifically, using the package rChartsDygraphs,
https://github.com/danielkrizian/rChartsDygraphs
and the following code:
#ui.r
####
require(shiny);require(rCharts);require(rChartsDygraph)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel('Dygraphs Test in Shiny with rCharts'),
  mainPanel(
    chartOutput('mygraph', 'dygraph', package="rChartsDygraph", add_lib=T)
  )
))
###
##server.r
require(rCharts);require(rChartsDygraph);require(shiny);require(quantmod)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
  getSymbols("SPY", from = "1993-01-01")
  SPY <- data.frame(Date=index(SPY), Price=SPY$SPY.Close)
  SPY$Momentum20days <- momentum(SPY$SPY.Close, 20)/lag(SPY$SPY.Close, 20)*100

  output$mygraph <- renderChart2({
    dygraph(data=SPY[,c("Date","SPY.Close")], width=800)
  })
})
###
on shiny-server v1.1.0.0 is causing repainting issues when one zooms into or pans the graph.

Interestingly, if the app is run locally with runApp() or runGist() the same issues do not appear.

Any thoughts on what is happening within shiny-server?

messages.subject: Re: In shiny debug mode, unable to print variables to screen as of shiny 0.10 onwards?
messages.subject_clean: In shiny debug mode, unable to print variables to screen as of shiny 0.10 onwards?
messages.body_plain:
Whenever I've found myself in this situation with Shiny it's because the browser() call is inside of a call to renderPrint(), either directly or indirectly. The way renderPrint works is by wrapping your expression in capture.output(), which diverts all standard output to a buffer. It looks like what's new with Shiny 0.10 is that renderPlot now uses capture.output as well, a little too aggressively.

You can break out of the capture.output() from within the browser() by using sink(), as long as you don't mind the renderPrint() missing the rest of your output. Alternatively, you can do cat("message\n", file=stderr()) to bypass the capture.output() and go to the console for a single message.

We'll get the renderPlot part fixed for Shiny 0.10.1 which we're hoping to ship in the coming weeks. Thanks for the bug report!

messages.subject: Re: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
messages.subject_clean: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
messages.body_plain:
I have isolated the sources of two confounding problems.

First, it is definitely something with the shinyAce package that no longer is working on Spark, but does work on other systems. Commenting out anything to do with rgl had no effect on any plots, rgl-related or otherwise. Only when I commented out the shinyAce code displays in my main panel 'R Code' tab panel did all the plots begin working again. The app also loads visibly more properly (with shinyAce active, my sidebar input controls flash in 'classic' view, then vanish and properly reappear in 'Selectize' format. This load and reload does not occur with shinyAce code commented out.).

So one problem I need to solve is why I can use shinyAce on our webserver but not on Spark, in the context I am using it. There were prior issues, but they were resolved (it worked with websockets off, so it used to work on Spark where websockets are disabled by default, but not on our own server, until I turned off websockets). Now with websockets off on both servers, it continues to work on our hosted server, but no longer on Spark.

The second issue relates to rgl. Now that I can at least see the plots again with shinyAce code commented out, I can see that all plots work except for rgl which fails to load. Previously, I found instructions to use:
options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) at the top of server.R
to enable rgl to work with Shiny apps. Which it did. Now it must be failing to load for some new reason.

Matt

messages.body_plain:
I got it working. It seems like it might be related to options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) mentioned under "running headless" in the shinyRGL doc. http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shinyRGL/README.html.

The strange thing is that we had the option line in server.R before library(shinyRGL), and it was working fine yesterday. It seems like after I installed ggvis, it stopped working. I added the following lines in ui.R, restarted the server, and updated some toolboxes, and it started working. Unfortunately, I'm not sure which thing I did fixed the problem.

options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE)

library(shinyRGL)

library(rgl)
I wonder if there's some kind of cross talk between apps. I thought I read somewhere that Shiny Server is efficient in recycling R processes . For example, if one app somehow happened to load RGL without this option set (for example, does loading ggvis in turns loads RGL, but doesn’t have the option set?). Then when the ECG app starts there’s already an R process running that already loaded the RGL library without the option set.

Is there some way I can force R to reload shinyRGL and RGL with the option set?

Jonathan

Shiny Server will not recycle R processes for different applications -- each application gets its own isolated process. I'll chew on this a little more and let you know if I think of anything.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Reactive error
messages.subject_clean: Reactive error
messages.body_plain:
The problem is in your switch statements. As inputs change over time, Shiny forces you to only use them in reactive expressions or observers, which in turn means that you'll always be using the most recent data unless you put guards against that. You have to wrap your switch statements in reactive({}) :

                   data <- reactive({switch(input$parameters,
                   "University Classes" = classes$Type
                     )})

Read up on reactivity if you haven't already and can spare the time: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html

> Whenever I've found myself in this situation with Shiny it's because the browser() call is inside of a call to renderPrint(), either directly or indirectly. The way renderPrint works is by wrapping your expression in capture.output(), which diverts all standard output to a buffer. It looks like what's new with Shiny 0.10 is that renderPlot now uses capture.output as well, a little too aggressively.

messages.subject: Re: Making a reactive variable wait for observe to finish?
messages.subject_clean: Making a reactive variable wait for observe to finish?
messages.body_plain:
You could give the database-mutating observer a higher priority (see ?observe). Anything higher than 0 should work.

Keep in mind that you're not setting the observer to a higher priority than the reactive(); it doesn't make sense to talk about reactive expressions having priorities, since they are lazily evaluated (whereas observers are eagerly executed). Rather, you're setting the observer to a higher priority than the observer that invokes your renderDataTable, which in turn invokes the reactive. The observers that drive outputs always have priority 0 unless you change them using outputOptions().

messages.subject: Re: action button auto reset
messages.subject_clean: action button auto reset
messages.body_plain:
The problem isn't that you need to reset the action button. This code works, changed lines in bold (and I also deleted the "data" reactive):

library(shiny)
runApp(list(ui = fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Create Factors App"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("data", label = "Data set",
        choices = c("mtcars", "faithful", "iris")),
      uiOutput("datafactor_ui")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      h4("Data Information"),
      verbatimTextOutput("datastr"),
      tableOutput("table")
    )
  )
),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$datafactor_ui <- renderUI({
      wellPanel(
        h5("Factor Variable:"),
        selectInput("factor", "", c("NULL", names(rslt$dat))),
        radioButtons('factlevel', 'Factor level',
          c(Default='asis',
            'As data order'='asdata',
            'Specified order'='speciord'),
          'asis'),
        textInput("ordlevl", "", value = ""),
        helpText("Enter levels such as Y, C, B etc.."),
        checkboxInput("ordfct", "Ordered Factor?", value = FALSE),
        actionButton("fctrun", "Run"))
    }) # end of output$datafactor_ui

    rslt <- reactiveValues()
    observe({
      rslt$dat <- get(input$data, 'package:datasets')
    })

    observe({ # For make factors in the data
      if (is.null(input$fctrun) || input$fctrun == 0)

        return()

      isolate({
        lvelord <- sub(" ","", unlist(strsplit(input$ordlevl, ",")))
        if (input$factor != "NULL") {
          rslt$dat[,input$factor] <- switch(input$factlevel,
            "asis"=factor(rslt$dat[,input$factor]),
            "asdata"=factor(rslt$dat[,input$factor],
              levels=unique(rslt$dat[,input$factor])),
            "speciord"= factor(rslt$dat[,input$factor], levels=lvelord))
          if (input$ordfct) rslt$dat[,input$factor] <- ordered(rslt$dat[,input$factor])
        }
      }) # end of isolate
    }) # end of observe
    output$datastr <- renderPrint({
      str(rslt$dat)
    })
    output$table <- renderTable({
      head(rslt$dat)
    })
  }
))

messages.subject: Re: tags$head() empty
messages.subject_clean: tags$head() empty
messages.body_plain:
You were not doing anything worng. It is a matter of printing. I guess
the printing function in shiny/htmltools was designed to print the
HTML body. The HTML head is extracted and rendered separately when an
HTML page is to be rendered, because we normally only see the HTML
body. This does not mean tags$head() is essentially different with
tags$style(): both are essentially lists, and it is just their printed
representations that are different. If you are interested in playing
with the HTML head, you can take a look at htmltools::renderTags.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Shiny : reactive variable with multiple dependencies
messages.subject_clean: Shiny : reactive variable with multiple dependencies
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Below I've included a server.r and ui.r file.  The design of the program is to generate a user-specificied number of entries (n()) from a population (also user specified) (N()).  The program should then highlight the selected tiles and display a list of the chosen tiles below.  Eventually, I hope to be able to contain a history of these entries (the samps variable is currently keeping track: on line 69 -- paste(c("Sample: ", sort(tail(samps, n())))) can be converted to paste(c("Sample: ",samps ))).

When this program is run, sometimes it seems that samps has an entry added to it and then is written to output, while at other times it seems that samps is written, and then an entry is appended.  Is there a way to force the appending to occur before the writing.  There might be some helpful code on 26-29, but I don't entirely understand its functionality.

Furthermore, in the ideal world, samps would be reset to an empty list when the user changes either or both of the sample size or the population size, so I set up an observe function at the end to try to do this.

Any help or pointers would be much appreciated!

#######################################
#######################################

SERVER.R

#######################################
#######################################

library("ggplot2")
library("shiny")

#runGitHub("shiny-examples", "rstudio", subdir = "012-datatables")
## predefining positions
#get.perm <- function(seed, pop.size) {
#  set.seed(seed)
#  sample(1:pop.size)
#}

ncols <- 10 #defaults to 10 columns in the display population
samps <<- c() # will hold the samples

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  ## define population
  #grab values
  N <- reactive(input$N)
  n <- reactive(input$n)
  #####
  #caculate number of rows/columns
  ncols.pop <- reactive(c(10,20,40,60)[(c(0,100,400,800) < N()) & (N() <= c(100,400,800,1000))])
  nrows.pop <- reactive(ceiling(N()/ncols.pop()))

  #set up the variable go to be in a position to keep track of dirty flags
  values <- reactiveValues(go = TRUE)
  session$onFlushed(function() {
    values$go <- FALSE
  })

  #this will go and eventually draw our population
  grid.pop <- reactive({
    if (input$sample==0) { #if submit button has not been pressed
      return(data.frame(expand.grid(x=1:ncols.pop(),y=nrows.pop():1)[1:input$N,],
                        label=1:input$N, sampled="FALSE"))
    }
    #if the button has been pressed
    samps <<- c(samps, sample(1:N(), n(), replace=FALSE))
    data.frame(expand.grid(x=1:ncols.pop(),y=nrows.pop():1)[1:N(),], label=1:N(), sampled=1:N() %in% tail(samps, n()))
  })

  ## output population plot
  output$popplot <- renderPlot({

    plot <- ggplot(grid.pop(),aes(x=x, y=y, label=label, fill=sampled)) +
      geom_tile(color="black", size=1.3, alpha=0.8, show_guide=FALSE) +
      geom_text(size=5, show_guide=FALSE) +
      labs(title="Population") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(text=element_text(size=24),
            panel.grid = element_blank(),
            panel.border = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank()
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values=c("lightblue","lightgreen"))

    print(plot)
  })

  ##caption text
  output$sample <- renderText({
    if (values$go) #check for dirty flag
      return(NULL)
    else{
      #don't display things that don't exist!
      if (input$sample == 0) return("Sample: ")
      paste(c("Sample: ", sort(tail(samps, n()))))
    }
  })

  observe({
    input$n
    input$N
    samps <<- c()
  })
})

#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################

UI.R

#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################
#######################################

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("Random Sample"),
    sidebarPanel(
          wellPanel(
            helpText(""),
            numericInput("N", "Select Population Size", min=1, max=1000, value=20, step = 1)
            ),
          wellPanel(
            helpText(""),
            numericInput("n", "Select Sample Size", min=1, max=999, value=4, step = 1),
            actionButton("sample", "Sample", icon = icon("refresh"))
            )
        ),  #end sidebar panel

    mainPanel(
    plotOutput("popplot"),
    h4(textOutput("sample"))
        ) #end mainpanel
))
